headline: Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud with massive memory bandwidth
summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is now offering standalone Nvidia Vera CPU instances, boasting up to 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth, significantly outperforming x86 competitors in benchmarks.
details: Nvidia and Oracle have officially announced the general availability of Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Superclusters. This move marks Nvidia's first standalone CPU deployment in a major hyperscale data center, positioning Vera against traditional x86 processors.

While not intended to replace x86 entirely, Vera's architecture offers distinct advantages for specific workloads, particularly in the burgeoning field of agentic AI. Its memory system is capable of an impressive 1.2 TB/s bandwidth, a critical factor for AI tasks involving large databases and extensive documentation.

Independent benchmarks show Nvidia's Vera CPU more than doubling the memory bandwidth of a dual Intel Xeon 6 system. This superior performance is attributed to its use of LPDDR5X-9600 memory, a monolithic die, and a distributed mesh for caching, which allows for higher memory bandwidth by optimizing process distribution.

The performance gains are also evident in Python workloads, which are foundational to many AI applications and agentic frameworks like CrewAI and LangGraph. Vera's efficiency in handling these Python-based tasks further solidifies its potential in the AI infrastructure landscape.

Oracle's integration of standalone Vera instances signifies a broader implication for data center CPU competition. By offering Vera alongside its existing Ampere Altra Arm-based instances, OCI is expanding its AI-focused compute options to cater to evolving demands in the AI sector.

topic: massive ai supercomputer listed on ebay
headline_marked: IT vendor lists [[$60 million AI supercomputer]] on eBay with 300 racks of GPUs
headline: IT vendor lists $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 300 racks of GPUs
summary: A 300-rack AI supercomputer featuring 9,600 Nvidia A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC processors is available for purchase on eBay for $59.7 million.
details: An IT vendor has listed a massive AI supercomputer for sale on eBay, with a price tag of $59.7 million. The system comprises 300 server racks and boasts an impressive 9,600 Nvidia A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome processors.

Each rack is equipped with four compute nodes and three management nodes. The compute nodes feature dual AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, eight Nvidia A100 40GB SXM4 accelerators, and 1TB of DDR4 memory, while management nodes include dual EPYC 64-core chips and 192GB of DDR4 memory.

The total cluster capacity reaches up to 268,800 cores and 1.4 petabytes of memory. While newer architectures like Nvidia's Blackwell and AMD's EPYC Turin are available, the A100 accelerators and EPYC Rome processors remain highly relevant for many AI and machine learning tasks, offering a more budget-friendly alternative to the latest hardware.

The listing includes options for free local pickup or FedEx Ground delivery, with expedited shipping available for $25 (two-day) or $50 (overnight). The seller, Core 4 Solutions, is reportedly seeing interest, with one buyer already having the item in their cart.
